name: 7.4 Confidence Interval (Home Costs) - Lab
_note: Built 2026-08-12. All ten authored fresh (lab kind): q28-name-the-four-pieces, q29-home-summary-stats, q30-home-standard-error, q31-home-90-interval, q32-home-alpha-tails, q33-count-inside-interval, q34-interpret-the-home-interval, q35-four-confidence-levels, q36-ebm-trend, pre-frq-grade-a-home-costs-interval. Points 10x10 = 100. BookSHelf 7.4 is a lab: collect 35 home sale prices from a newspaper, compute the sample mean and standard deviation, build a t-interval (sigma unknown, so 7.2's machinery applies), interpret it, and fill a table of intervals at four confidence levels. The MOM assignment checks the numbers on the section's OWN demonstration dataset (Table 7.4.1: 35 sorted prices, sum $14,350,000, sum of squares 6,317,692 x 10^6, so x-bar = $410,000, s ~ $113,006, n = 35, df = 34), which is fixed - so every answer is deterministic. Lab settings per reference/intro-stats-assessment-settings.md: 3 attempts x 20 versions, no penalty, no early-finish bonus, GROUP gradebook category, 2 late passes, no time limit. Pre-FRQ is authored-first (no lab FRQ to mirror): categories State the Sample Summary (3) / Build the Interval (3) / Interpret in Context (4), dropped category BUILD THE INTERVAL - deliberately DIFFERENT from the 4.4/4.6/5.3/6.4 lab pre-FRQs' drops (State the Theoretical Value / State the Empirical Value / Compare and Explain the Gap) and from 7.1/7.2/7.3's (Confidence Level Meaning / Assessing the Claim / Statistical Decision), since the template forbids repeating a dropped category.

questions.title: Name the Four Pieces - population, sample, parameter, and statistic
The Home Summary Statistics - x-bar, s, and n of the 35 prices
The Home 90% Interval - EBM, lower and upper endpoints
The Home Alpha and Tails - alpha = 0.10 and alpha/2 = 0.05
Count Inside the Interval - 9 of 35 prices, about 25.7%
Interpret the Home Interval - the specific sentence, the general sentence, and the bad reading
The Four Confidence Levels - the EBM at 50%, 80%, 95%, and 99%
The EBM Trend - what happens to the error bound and the width as the confidence level rises
Pre-FRQ Grade a Home Costs Interval - a home-sale-price scenario with a grading checklist, where the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
